description: Golden vector table for the shared `hittable` predicate (#1933, #2891), for input shapes the fixed 320x240 fold fixture in ios-snapshot-engine-conformance.json cannot reach. RULE: a node is actionable when it is enabled, its own rect passes the box guard below, and its center falls inside the viewport box, half-open on the right and bottom edges. BOX GUARD: a box is usable when all four components are finite, both extents (x+width, y+height) are finite, the size is positive, and it is not CGRect.infinite — whose components and extents are all finite, so only identity refuses it. SnapshotGeometry.isPositiveFinite (Swift) and isPositiveFiniteRect in packages/kernel/src/rect.ts are the twins that enforce exactly this, one per language. Implementations of the predicate: SnapshotGeometry.isGeometricallyActionable (Swift, replayed by ActionabilityPolicyTests) and isGeometricallyActionable in packages/kernel/src/rect.ts (replayed by scripts/ios-snapshot-differential.test.ts). The viewport is the declared fact `reported`, `derived`, or `missing` (IosViewportEvidence); a box the guard refuses never becomes `reported`. `hittable: null` is the absent bit: with no viewport box, containment is undecided, while a disabled or degenerate node is still a declared `false` because that half of the rule needs no box. Every row declares `swift` and `typescript` and at least one must run it; a row one side skips carries `asymmetry`.

cases.name: a center strictly inside the reported box is actionable
a center one point short of the right edge is actionable
a center landing exactly on the right edge is not actionable: the edge is half-open
a center one point short of the bottom edge is actionable
a center landing exactly on the bottom edge is not actionable: the edge is half-open
a center landing exactly on the left edge is actionable: that edge is inclusive
a center landing exactly on the top edge is actionable: that edge is inclusive
a disabled node is not actionable even with its center inside the box
a center inside the box reached through a canonical box is actionable
the same center reached through a negative width is not actionable: the node guard decides, and Swift used to answer actionable
a center inside the box reached through a zero width is not actionable
that zero-area box's center reached through a canonical box is actionable
Apple's no-box sentinel is not actionable on either language: its components and extents are all finite and its center is (0,0), so the box guard refuses it by value in both
finite components can still spell an unmeasurable box: the box overflows its own right edge out to infinity, so the extent check refuses it

a node rect whose components are not finite is refused by the box guard before any center is computed; the bridge decoder refuses to decode such a frame earlier still, so this row pins the guard and not a producer
the center a box spelled infinite lands on is actionable when a real box reaches it
the same node whose center sits inside a reported box has no hittable bit once the viewport goes missing
cases.asymmetry: The TypeScript predicate takes a box. Without one, each host path withholds the bit before asking it: the bridge reader publishes derived hittability only for a reported viewport, and resolveViewportEvidence refuses to fold a regular presentation.

cases.name: a viewport declared invalid leaves the bit absent the same way
cases.asymmetry: The TypeScript predicate takes a box. Without one, each host path withholds the bit before asking it: the bridge reader publishes derived hittability only for a reported viewport, and resolveViewportEvidence refuses to fold a regular presentation.

cases.name: a disabled node is not actionable without a viewport: that half of the rule needs no box
cases.asymmetry: The TypeScript predicate takes a box. Without one, each host path withholds the bit before asking it: the bridge reader publishes derived hittability only for a reported viewport, and resolveViewportEvidence refuses to fold a regular presentation.

cases.name: a zero-area node is not actionable without a viewport: the node guard needs no box
cases.asymmetry: The TypeScript predicate takes a box. Without one, each host path withholds the bit before asking it: the bridge reader publishes derived hittability only for a reported viewport, and resolveViewportEvidence refuses to fold a regular presentation.

cases.name: a derived box the capture read from its own root still answers containment
a derived box still refuses a node whose center is off that box
